about: The sweep of the Milky Way's plane for infrared sources that appeared between SPHEREx's visits: its 14 survivors, copied from docs/sweep/summary.json and docs/sweep.md by scripts/export_anomalies.py. 'candidate' means a source we found in no catalogue or report we checked; nobody has confirmed it and nothing has been reported.
visits: August to September 2025, February to April 2026, August to September 2026

survivors.label: A
survivors.allowed_sentence: Candidate A, an infrared source in Sagittarius, was too faint to detect in SPHEREx images from late August and early September 2025 and was more than 100 times brighter by late March 2026; it is a candidate that we found in no catalogue or report we checked, and nobody has confirmed it yet.
survivors.last_non_detection: 2025-09-10 09:53 UT, below about 14 mJy at 4.4-5.0 micrometres
survivors.rise: more than 100 times within SPHEREx (at least about 170 on the fits, at least 60 without a model); at least about 500 times NEOWISE W2 (2014-2024), 1,000 times Spitzer GLIMPSE II [4.5] (2005-06) and 300 times VVV Ks (2010-2019)

visits_d6.text: not detected: -5.5, -4.3 and -2.4 +/- 2.8 mJy in three fits with the neighbour modelled; upper limit about 10-14 mJy (about 40 mJy with no model)

survivors.label: B
survivors.allowed_sentence: Candidate B, an infrared source in Scorpius, was too faint to detect in SPHEREx images from August and September 2025, had appeared by late February 2026 and was at least 250 times brighter by August 2026; it is a candidate that we found in no catalogue or report we checked, and nobody has confirmed it yet.
survivors.rise: at least 250 times from August 2025 to August 2026 (at least about 100 to March 2026); at least about 700 times NEOWISE W2 (2024-03-09), 1,400 times Spitzer [4.5] (2004 and 2012) and 400 times VVV Ks (inferred, not measured at the spot)

visits_d6.text: not detected: 0.28, -0.5 +/- 1.1 and -0.75 +/- 1.6 mJy in three fits; 3-sigma limit 2.5-4.0 mJy
393-424 mJy, rising about 10 per cent a day

survivors.label: C
survivors.allowed_sentence: Candidate C, an infrared source in Norma, was too faint to detect in SPHEREx images from July and August 2025, was at least 30 times brighter in late February and early March 2026 and had faded again by August 2026; its light hints at a nova hidden behind the Milky Way's dust, but it is a candidate that we found in no catalogue or report we checked, and nobody has confirmed it yet.
survivors.last_non_detection: 2025-08-19 22:57 UT, below about 3 mJy at 4-5 micrometres
survivors.rise: at least about 30 times in its continuum within SPHEREx; at least about 20 times NEOWISE (2010-2024), 270 times GLIMPSE I [4.5], 560 times Deep GLIMPSE, 380 times APOGLIMPSE and 340 times VVV Ks

survivors.why: 39 mJy against 1.4 in a 4-image comparison, but the all-exposure medians of D6 are 4, 15 and 2 mJy and D5 negative: 5 sigma at most, not confirmed. A methanol maser and sub-millimetre clump lie 8 arcseconds away, so it may be worth a look by someone who knows that region.

its brightness in the tile images swung (136, 126, 23, 116, 125) but the median of all 3.8 to 5 micrometre exposures is 143, 135 and 157 mJy in D5 and 111, 96 and 118 in D6: steady. One tile image was measured on a crowded background.
the catalogued planetary nebula PN M 1-40 lies 0.7 arcseconds away; NEOWISE saw it steady (21 visits, 1.05 times); all-exposure medians 96, 86, 178 mJy in D6. A bright nebula, not a transient.
